sources.title: Connected Nations Spring 2026
facts: The Spring 2026 report describes fixed and mobile coverage using a January 2026 reference snapshot.
Full-fibre coverage reached about 24.9 million UK residential premises and gigabit-capable coverage reached 89%.
Ofcom estimated around 4,000 premises could be eligible for the affordable decent-broadband Universal Service Obligation.
Predicted geographic 4G coverage from at least one operator was about 96%.
Coverage, take-up, satellite affordability and predicted mobile availability are separate concepts.

sources.title: Mobile connectivity you can count on
facts: Ofcom published the discussion document on 3 June 2026.
It distinguishes reliable user experience from modelled coverage predictions.
The document calls for coordinated action across operators, government, transport bodies and local stakeholders.
Responses were requested by 5pm on 29 July 2026, with an update planned for early 2027.
Its evidence bundle includes consumer research, Manchester work and train-connectivity research rather than parcel observations.

sources.title: Mobile signal and connectivity on train journeys
facts: The train-connectivity research was published on 3 June 2026.
It examined 24 rail-route segments using sampled journeys.
A good connection was defined using at least 5 Mbit/s download, 1.5 Mbit/s upload and 50 ms latency.
Poor connectivity was observed for between 58% and 83% of measured journey time depending on operator.
Sampled train journeys cannot be treated as universal geographic or address-level coverage.

sources.title: Map Your Mobile reaches one million users
facts: Ofcom announced the one-million-user milestone on 29 May 2026.
The service allows postcode-based comparison of predicted mobile coverage and performance.
It combines operator predictions with crowdsourced Opensignal measurements.
Postal-district experience scores are distinct from individual-premise guarantees.
A checker result must retain operator, postcode, measurement type and observation vintage.

sources.title: Shared Rural Network wellbeing and social value baseline survey
facts: The baseline survey was published on 15 January 2026.
Ipsos surveyed 1,285 residents, households and businesses in SRN beneficiary locations.
The study concerns wellbeing, social value and lived experience rather than engineering coverage measurement.
Beneficiary-area sampling does not prove signal availability at every premise.
Baseline survey results require geography, sample and survey-date preservation.

sources.title: Mobile Supplier Additionality research
facts: The supplier-additionality research was published on 15 January 2026 and produced by FarrPoint.
It examines how the number of available mobile operators affects consumer and economic benefits.
The modelling tests equal incremental changes in operator availability.
It considers both commercial and publicly supported rural 4G investment.
Modelled additionality is not evidence of current service at a specific property.

sources.title: Ofcom Annual Report and Accounts 2025-26
facts: Ofcom published the annual-report downloads on 10 July 2026.
The report records mmWave spectrum awards covering 68 high-density areas.
It describes decisions enabling direct-to-device satellite services.
It also records plans concerning mobile and Wi-Fi spectrum sharing.
Regulatory decisions and spectrum capability do not establish deployed service at an individual property.

sources.title: Preparing internet-connected devices for the 2G and 3G switch-off
facts: Ofcom updated the IoT and connected-device guidance on 19 June 2026.
UK operators had completed their 3G switch-offs while 2G retirement dates vary by operator.
The guidance references EE in May 2029, O2 in summer 2029 and Vodafone in 2030.
Device suppliers are expected to plan continuity and address roaming-SIM risks.
Transition guidance is not evidence of coverage quality or availability at a premise.

sources.title: What the 2G and 3G switch-off means for consumers
facts: The consumer guidance was updated on 29 May 2026.
It explains that UK 3G networks have closed while 2G retirement will occur later.
Most 4G and 5G devices are not expected to require hardware replacement solely because of the switch-off.
Older devices, alarms, meters and roaming arrangements can require action.
Technology transition status must not be interpreted as a local signal measurement.

sources.title: Industry expectations for the 2G and 3G switch-off
facts: Ofcom updated its industry expectations on 29 May 2026.
All four UK mobile operators had completed their 3G switch-offs.
Providers are expected to communicate clearly, treat customers fairly and preserve access to essential services.
Operator 2G retirement windows and migration safeguards are documented separately.
Consumer-protection expectations are not parcel-level connectivity data.

sources.title: Premises unable to receive 30 Mbit/s broadband
sources.lines: indicator definition, January 2026 vintage and downloads
facts: The indicator measures the percentage of premises unable to receive download speeds above 30 Mbit/s.
The observation vintage is January 2026 and the indicator was published on 13 May 2026.
The displayed geography is lower-tier or unitary authority.
Downloads are provided in CSV, CSVW and spreadsheet formats.
ONS warns that aggregation can produce differences from other published figures.
